I have been attending Clarence Street Snap Fitness and the space lacks cleanliness and is sadly filthy. Gym is meant to bring health and positive aspects to our life.

I was a previous member at Snap fitness in Perth, where the situation was very different and have moved to Sydney in the last 2 weeks. The Clarence Street location was the most convenient for me to attend.

I tried to the manager (whom is hardly ever at the reception desk and only found exercising) as to work with improvements for a filthy environment is unacceptable.

The gym has no soaps in most of the toilet sinks, stations where wipes are located is super dirty around… the other day there was not a single alcohol gel bottle filled to be used. Dust is everywhere especially weight sections. This week the stair climber equipment has a spider web right in front, with a spider hanging there.

The manager asked me to send him an e-mail yesterday, which I did. I wrote and included pictures as to the matter.  I wasn´t comfortable with the fact that I had already spoken and no one else was in copy as to address the issue. The manager replied to my e-mail on the same day, informing those actions would be taken, but on the following day I was surprised with an unexpected incident today towards me.

Today, I was surprised with a rude approach from one member, which and opted not to reply and continued with my music and exercise. I didn´t respond and wished the man “all the best” when we left the gym at the same time. Latter that day the same manager sent me an e-mail filled with lies as if I was the one with inappropriate behavior in the gym, when I was the one who received an unexpected attitude when returning the man´s towel.  The manager wrote that I had inappropriate behavior at the gym, to members and staff members. That I was no longer welcome at the gym. This is a lie and didn´t occurred at all!!

I am surprises and shocked with these two incidents which apparently might be connected… I felt so unsafe today. I was the only women and was mistreated and later received an email filled with lies. I only wanted to use one of the 3 benches, which 2 were being used and the third was occupied by his towel. I decided to wait and do another exercise. While I was doing a rep of 4x18, the man that left his towel at the beach only came once. Once I was finished, I literally went to him and ask if I could use the equipment. He said yes. Which was great. I had music on my ears and grab his towel to give it back to him. OMG! That guy, freaked out, he was so arrogant, saying he could grab the towel himself and that I was rude to touch his towel. He kept speaking rudely towards me (I felt harassed). That was just awful! I felt so mistreated by the tone of his voice and the way he kept speaking to me. I said I didn’t hear him and didn’t know it was rude to give the towel back to him. Afterward I only said: “you’re a very rude man, and I’m glad I’m not listening to you, as I have headphones on”. It was awful, really. I felt terrible and didn’t feel safe at all.

I am very surprised with this entire situation and neve had similar experience. I find this experience at this gym unacceptable.

All the best

I joined a kendo trial session here, and it was an amazing experience. The atmosphere was friendly and energetic, and the instructors and senior members were very supportive, even for complete beginners.

Kendo training here is well organized and gives you a real taste of discipline, spirit and traditional martial arts. I enjoyed it so much that I wanted to officially join the club. Unfortunately, I only had half a semester left, and kendo is a sport that really benefits from long-term commitment. If you want the full experience, I highly recommend having at least one full year to train, improve and participate in events.

The facilities in SUSF are spacious and clean, with proper flooring and equipment for many different sports. There are also many other clubs and fitness programs, so it’s a great place to stay active, meet new people and try something new.

Overall, I had a very positive experience here. What is most concerning is not a single maintenance issue or one-off closure—it’s the constant pattern of members paying premium prices while being repeatedly denied access to the facilities and amenities included in their membership.

The pool, spa and sauna area has become a perfect example. Last Saturday, the entire area was closed for the day because the club was understaffed. Today, the area was closed again well before the advertised closing time. The spa has also been unavailable for extended periods over the past six months due to renovations, broken pipes and other maintenance issues. Altogether, I estimate it has been out of service for well over a month during that period.

Even when the wellness area is open, staff have increasingly started cleaning and applying slippery chemicals up to 45 minutes before closing, despite the area officially remaining open to members. Guests are effectively being pushed out early because management has chosen operational convenience over member experience.

The gym floor itself is not much better. The upstairs cable fly machine has broken down repeatedly, multiple cardio machines are frequently out of service, and members are constantly dealing with construction works and restricted access to facilities. The climbing wall is being removed and replaced with office space, creating ongoing disruption, and now renovation works have extended onto the gym floor itself, with sections of the weights area blocked off during peak evening hours.

The Pilates studio air conditioning was also unreliable for an extended period, making classes uncomfortable and, at times, difficult to attend.

What makes all of this particularly frustrating is that membership fees continue to increase while the overall member experience continues to deteriorate. Equipment breaks down repeatedly, amenities are unavailable, facilities are closed due to staffing shortages, and construction works seem never-ending. Yet members continue to be charged premium prices for a service that is increasingly falling short of a premium standard.

I fully appreciate that maintenance, repairs and upgrades are sometimes necessary. However, the sheer volume of recurring issues points to a broader management problem rather than isolated incidents. There appears to be a lack of planning, accountability and operational oversight.

The staff on the floor are generally friendly and helpful, but they can only work with the resources and direction they’re given. The responsibility for the current state of the club sits with management.

I would welcome a response from senior or national management because, unfortunately, the examples above are only a portion of the issues members have been dealing with throughout the year. Virgin Active Pitt Street has enormous potential, but right now it is failing to deliver the premium experience that members are paying for.","Images":["https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/grass-cs/ACvplmPFc9BsQbmi-Rl1V7r0qHpwfUyd-ylLpnfi5YlX2upXXBw_csr8kx3sBPJm2492LOTYglxjI7UCflb6M9C9DjwfpGu_HENToIGnEc67m_3nbJaVCgoZ1AHZZsgVU0MUZNxeIpU3tRNQ5DDI=k-no","https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/grass-cs/ACvplmN7gV3vduM9_y9XKzjiKli3_QhewGqY6TNRLMmM-Oq-F82XwNbwVZewHdn1vNXgByPZLP4skPe2oBinMdZ0Lws1r0sN-nYsjLaFqdrQGXK4lhFlCRkkbGCwQh5rhJksen5L4NT-mRMuCI1x=k-no","https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/grass-cs/ACvplmPDgzNAvSQcFrmeCGTV0j3VIzU-CJdrNYL64XtbzxlNEKsETvlcXnIj3MnJ1zIwK5KZBYS1j4hiDFAnLXBlE4kHRaAmcsILLhAX__hFVfuTnkHBZmTC58e-CD3qaalUxEqlwUmpQXPDzpyr=k-no","https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/grass-cs/ACvplmM4zbcNsxD7Z7dMQJj7ziZd_CedrfJkM0JIlIFRlCoUFUrCHxKYIv7DuzlKDJAs5c5dIqgSxPJcRRxnsTYMCfKiPjQ6-2MzCZNdVtcAzGPGbu27t-uD_zrIiU_7rvwFRl_puG86qfuFXkQ=k-no"],"When":"3 months ago","review_id":"Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT2psdk1qZzRNV3c1V1dWTk5tVkdSV1o2UldVM1lsRRAB","source":"Google","rating_scale":5,"rating_float":2,"author_url":"https://www.google.com/maps/contrib/101128568016208249168/reviews?hl=en-GB","posted_at_unix_micros":1782211585544424,"updated_at_unix_micros":1782211585544424,"language":"en","translated_lang":"","text_original":"I’ve been a member of Virgin Active Pitt Street for almost three years, and I can honestly say that the club is currently being managed worse than at any point since I joined.

(I discovered this on my first trip back post renovation. the part your feet hook under is lose making the machine bias a single leg. when using the machine with both legs as intended, it's essentially unusable and probably dangerous.)

no air-conditioning. especially upstairs is appalling. it's somehow hotter inside than it is outside on some days. not to mention, the bathrooms consistently have a foul odour from what i assume is a ventilation issue.

the lower bathrooms lost their sanitation dispensers for wiping the seats for some reason.

a personal nitpick others might be fine with are the newly installed spotlights. they create an aesthetic well lit interior for promotional material but functionally, when you're working out and being blasted with a spotlight, it can be a distracting and unpleasent experience.

the most significant beneficial changes are the amenities/services added such as powerbanks, juice machine, massage areas, etc. but even these are either a paid add on or there to sell a product.

I could go on and on...

It's clear anytime used this renovation as an excuse to increase the price without properly evaluating the facilities or functionality of the gym. its a sloppy coat of paint so they can sell what on the outside may look like a "premium" gym.

If you value your health and want a good workout, then this is most definitely not the gym for you.

During Covid, I switched to a CrossFit gym and never went back to a regular box gym. The name can be intimidating but I assure you that one would get a more efficient and productive workout session. No wasted time waiting for equipment to be available. You will be in a class setting and your workout is timed. All you have to focus on is to power through the workout of the day.
I travel a lot for work and found CrossFit Athletic city next to my hotel. I just had to give them a try. They have a great gym set up, classes that challenge you to push yourself. Their facilities are comfortable and clean.
The coaches are very supportive and helpful.
I got to meet Pete, the owner. He s got great energy and very motivated in making sure members have a great gym session. I also met Maeva, one of the weekday coaches. [{"Name":"Angela Kim","ProfilePicture":"https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/a-/ALV-UjWO9yNcXz5itzvXUSxgAZegyhMkp6ZvfCDGcf17sf3e8hOo2ZO9Zg=s120-c-rp-mo-ba12-br100","Rating":5,"Description":"THE BEST GYM EVER!
I didn't have ANY fitness backgrounds when I joined CrossFit Sydney, and I have been training there for over 2 years and I can confidently say that I gain lots of knowledge and got to know myself better.
When I started CrossFit I was worried about getting injured or just intense workouts, BUT this gym absolutely changed my stereotype. Andrew and the coaches know what they are doing, and by following their instructions and knowing my limits, I haven't been injured or got too tired after workouts - I'm just naturally clumsy, so I sometimes got hurt outside  of the gym though.. I started from 35kg squat max, and now I can lift more than doubled weight. I can do pull ups, cleans, snatches, handstand, and other crazy things that I hadn't even thought about doing it!
I learnt a lot, laughed a lot, and lifted a lot. This gym made my life better, and I definitely want more people to enjoy this lifestyle. It's a shame that I need to leave the gym, as I'm leaving Sydney, but I would definitely come back when I come back to Australia.
